# Reverse String II.

@example The groups are "rhy", "thm" and "ic"; the 1st and the 3rd are reversed.
"rhythmic"
3
=> "yhrthmci"

@example The groups are "ju", "ke", "bo" and "x"; only the 1st and the 3rd are reversed.
"jukebox"
2
=> "ujkeobx"

@example k is more than the length, so the whole string is one group.
"quilt"
8
=> "tliuq"

# The smallest input.
"z"
1
=> "z"

# k at its largest, far beyond the length.
"wn"
10000
=> "nw"

# k = 1: every group is one character, so nothing changes.
"frog"
1
=> "frog"

# k equal to the length, and one less.
"plumb"
5
=> "bmulp"

"plumb"
4
=> "mulpb"

# One character short of two full groups: the second group stays.
"kitchen"
4
=> "ctikhen"

# Exactly two full groups, and two full groups and one character more.
"vexing"
3
=> "xeving"

"brought"
3
=> "orbught"

# Four full groups: the string ends with a group that stays as it is.
"wolfpackhunt"
3
=> "lowfpahkcunt"

# A 3rd group of k and a 4th of one character: only the 3rd is reversed.
"thunderstorms"
4
=> "nuhtdersmrots"

# A longer string: 1100 letters in groups of 7.
""
7
=> ""

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"ijkjhlllk"
10
=> "klllhjkji"

@gen 2 small
"hjkilik"
2
=> "jhkiilk"

@gen 3 small
"hhijkl"
7
=> "lkjihh"

@gen 4 small
"jlhk"
1
=> "jlhk"

@gen 5 small
"iijlllkili"
4
=> "ljiillkiil"

@gen 6 small
"lk"
1
=> "lk"

@gen 7 small
"lj"
1
=> "lj"

@gen 8 small
"ijlljhl"
2
=> "jillhjl"

# A full-size case from gen.c: 10^4 letters, the longest s can be, in
# groups of 2904. The 1st and the 3rd are reversed; the 2nd stays, and so
# does the 4th, the last 1288 letters.
@gen 23
""
2904
=> ""
